For generic $q$, or whenever the quantum integers needed for $p_r,p_s,p_t$ are units, the unnormalized trivalent theta pairing satisfies

$$\Theta(r,s,t)=\frac{[m]![n']![p]![m+n'+p+1]!}{[m+n']![n'+p]![m+p]!},$$

where $m=(r+s-t)/2$, $n'=(s+t-r)/2$, $p=(t+r-s)/2$ are nonnegative integers. The vertices and exact unit domain are those of [[lem-temperley-lieb-general-theta-net-evaluation]]. At $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and $0\le r,s,t\le\ell-2$, the pairing is positive when the triangle/parity conditions hold and $r+s+t\le2\ell-4$; it is zero for a triangle/parity triple above that level. A triple requiring an undefined root JW projector is not implicitly included.

Put $k=\ell-2$ and quotient the diagram category by the tensor ideal generated by $p_{k+1}$. A retained path of length $n$ is $a=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ with $a_0=0$, $0\le a_i\le k$ and $|a_i-a_{i-1}|=1$. There are inclusions $i_a:p_{a_n}\to n$ and retractions $r_a:n\to p_{a_n}$ such that $r_ai_b=0$ for distinct paths, $r_ai_a=p_{a_n}$, and $\sum_a i_ar_a=1_n$. Consequently the $E_{a,b}=i_ar_b$ at a common endpoint form complete matrix units, with

$$E_{a,b}E_{c,d}=\delta_{b,c}E_{a,d},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(E_{a,b})=\delta_{a,b}[a_n+1]_q.$$

Their pairing is nondegenerate. The endpoint $p_{k+1}$ is deleted before normalization; no denominator $[\ell]$ is used.

Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, $m=\ell-1$ and $f=p_m$. Put $B_n=\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ and

$$J_n=\begin{cases}0,&n<m,\\ B_n(f\otimes1_{n-m})B_n,&n\ge m.\end{cases}$$

If $\mathcal I$ is the categorical tensor ideal generated by $f$, then $\mathcal I(n,n)=J_n$ at every rank. Moreover $\operatorname{ptr}_n(J_n)\subseteq J_{n-1}$. Thus this single embedded two-sided ideal already contains every annular consequence with arbitrary external strands and cups/caps. Below the boundary its component is zero, including contractions given by a partial trace rather than an internal turnback.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, and suppose $[2],\ldots,[n]$ are units. The projector $p_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]] has coefficient $1$ on the identity diagram, is nonzero and idempotent, and is annihilated on both sides by each $U_i$ for $1\le i<n$. Its corner is $p_n\mathrm{TL}_n p_n=R p_n$, so it is the unique idempotent with identity coefficient $1$ and those two-sided annihilation conditions. For $n\ge1$,

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

For any commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and $n\ge0$, the unnormalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(yx),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)U_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$$

for $x,y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$, where $U_n$ is the cup-cap generator on the last two strands of $\mathrm{TL}_{n+1}$. For $x\in\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$ and $h\in\mathrm{TL}_n$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n\bigl(h(x\otimes1)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{ptr}_n(h)x\bigr).$$

No division by $\delta$ occurs.

In the pivotal setting of [[def-negligible-morphism-in-a-pivotal-category]], the negligible morphisms are closed under addition, scalar multiplication, arbitrary composition on either side, and tensor product on either side. Thus they form a two-sided tensor ideal. The proof uses an explicit partial-trace identity and does not assume that an arbitrary intertwiner of a tensor product factors as a tensor product of intertwiners.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. Define the quantum integers by

$$[0]_\delta=0,\qquad [1]_\delta=1,\qquad [r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta\quad(r\ge1).$$

The **quantum characteristic** of $(R,\delta)$ is the least positive integer $\ell$ with $[\ell]_\delta=0$, if one exists, and $\ell=\infty$ otherwise. No element of $R$ is inverted in this definition.

For $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, write $[r]_q=[r]_\delta$. If $q\ne\pm1$, this agrees with $(q^r-q^{-r})/(q-q^{-1})$; at $q=\pm1$ the recurrence gives $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}$. For complex-parameter classification, write $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$, with $\kappa=\infty$ when $q^2$ has infinite order. If $q\ne\pm1$, the quantum characteristic equals $\kappa$ when $\kappa<\infty$ and is $\infty$ otherwise. At $q=\pm1$, $\kappa=1$ but the complex quantum characteristic is $\infty$, because $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}\ne0$ for every positive $r$.

For a field $K$ of positive characteristic $p$, set $p(0)=1$ and, when $\ell<\infty$, set $p(i)=\ell p^{i-1}$ for $i\ge1$. In characteristic zero and finite $\ell$, the finite digit scale is $p(1)=\ell$; the separate characteristic-zero criterion below uses $a\ell-1$ for arbitrary positive integers $a$. If $\ell=\infty$, every finite index is already in the range $n<\ell$.

Initially let $q$ be an indeterminate, let $[j]=q^{j-1}+q^{j-3}+\cdots+q^{1-j}$ for $j\ge1$, let $[0]!=1$, and set $\delta=q+q^{-1}$. For nonnegative integers $m,n,p$, put
$$r=m+p,\qquad s=m+n,\qquad t=n+p,\qquad h=m+n+p.$$
Equivalently, $(r,s,t)$ satisfies the triangle inequalities and even-sum condition, with $m=(r+s-t)/2$, $n=(s+t-r)/2$, and $p=(t+r-s)/2$. All Jones–Wenzl projectors below have identity coefficient one and are unnormalized.

Let $W_m:0\to2m$ be $m$ nested cups, whose outputs are two consecutive $m$-strand bundles: cup $i$ joins position $i$ of the first bundle to position $m+1-i$ of the second. Let $B_m:2m\to0$ be its horizontal reflection. Define
$$A=1_p\otimes W_m\otimes1_n:t\longrightarrow r+s,\qquad B=1_p\otimes B_m\otimes1_n:r+s\longrightarrow t,$$
$$\alpha=(p_r\otimes p_s)Ap_t,\qquad \beta=p_tB(p_r\otimes p_s),\qquad \Theta(m,n,p)=\operatorname{Tr}_t(\beta\alpha).$$
Thus the pairwise bundles at each trivalent vertex have sizes $m,n,p$: there are $m$ strands between arms $r,s$, $n$ between arms $s,t$, and $p$ between arms $t,r$. This fixes the vertex without a further scalar normalization. The theta net has the three JW-labelled edges $r,s,t$, since idempotence collapses the doubled projectors. Its value is
$$\Theta(m,n,p)=\frac{[m]![n]![p]![h+1]!}{[m+n]![n+p]![m+p]!}.$$
For $p\ge1$ the closed-diagram strip recurrence is
$$[m+p][n+p]\Theta(m,n,p)=[p][m+n+p+1]\Theta(m,n,p-1),\qquad \Theta(m,n,0)=[m+n+1].$$

These identities specialize to every complex $q\ne0$ for which $[j]\ne0$ for $1\le j\le M=\max(r,s,t)$, using the Laurent-polynomial convention at $q=\pm1$. These hypotheses construct the three projectors and make every displayed denominator a unit; $[h+1]$ need not be nonzero. In particular, if $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and $0\le r,s,t\le\ell-2$, then $\Theta>0$ when $h\le\ell-2$, whereas $\Theta=0$ when $h\ge\ell-1$. The latter vertex has zero trace pairing against every reverse morphism. No undefined higher root projector or $0/0$ convention is used.

derivations.claim: Write $m=\ell-1$ and $p=p_m$. It is a nonzero idempotent with one-dimensional corner and trace $[\ell]=0$ by [F3,F4]. If an element has a nonzero coefficient at $E_{a,b}$, multiplying by $E_{b,a}$ detects it in this nonzero weighted matrix-trace pairing. The quotient trace pairing is therefore nondegenerate. Together with step 1.1 this proves $I_n=\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)$ and the full matrix-block description. Inserting the path decompositions on both ends describes every unequal-degree Hom space as the corresponding rectangular matrix blocks; its pairing with the reverse Hom space is also nondegenerate. Thus the categorical negligible ideal is precisely the boundary tensor ideal, not a larger ideal known only on endomorphisms. The endpoint corners are $\mathbb Cp_c$, so its additive Karoubi quotient is semisimple with exactly the stated simple labels.

Sandwich a basis matching from $c$ to $a+b$ between $p_c$ and $p_a\otimes p_b$. Any arc joining two points of the same labelled arm is killed by its innermost adjacent turnback. A remaining matching must have the three bundle sizes $(a+b-c)/2$, $(b+c-a)/2$, $(c+a-b)/2$, so it exists only for a triangle/parity triple and is unique. Thus this projected Hom space is spanned by the vertex of [F5], and its reverse by the reflected vertex. Their trace pairing is the exact theta scalar. When the labels are retained, [F5] makes it positive exactly for $a+b+c\le2\ell-4$ and zero above that level. Step 2.1 identifies quotient Hom with this pairing modulo its radical, so its dimension is respectively one or zero. No theta value is divided at a forbidden level.

All endpoint projectors up to $p_m$ are nonzero by their identity coefficient. The matching-turnback corner calculation gives full matrix units just as before, now including the endpoint $m$; their completeness is the unreduced JW split. Hence $\mathrm{TL}_m$ is semisimple. The endpoint-$m$ block has the unique all-up path and is $\mathbb Cp_m$. Its trace weight is $[m+1]=0$, whereas every other endpoint weight is positive. Thus precisely this one-dimensional block is the trace radical, while semisimplicity makes the Jacobson radical zero. This proves the boundary assertion directly, without assuming a later ordinary semisimplicity criterion.

Fix an integer $\ell\ge3$ and set $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, so the multiplicative order of $q^2$ is $\ell$. Use the divided-power integral form of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] from [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], specialized by $v\mapsto q$ to $\mathbb C$. In type $A_1$, write $K=K_h$ and $E,F$ for the rank-one generators. The convention is

$$KEK^{-1}=q^2E,\qquad KFK^{-1}=q^{-2}F,\qquad [E,F]=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}},$$

$$\Delta(K)=K\otimes K,\qquad \Delta(E)=E\otimes K+1\otimes E,\qquad \Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K^{-1}\otimes F.$$

This is the Sawin coproduct, rather than the inverse-$K$ coproduct in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Its counit is $\varepsilon(K)=1$, $\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon(F)=0$ and its antipode is $S(E)=-EK^{-1}$, $S(F)=-KF$, $S(K)=K^{-1}$. The exact integral transport is from the library algebra with opposite coproduct, by $E_{\rm target}=KE_{\rm lib}$, $F_{\rm target}=F_{\rm lib}K^{-1}$ and $K_{\rm target}=K_{\rm lib}$. Substituting these generators gives the displayed coproduct and unchanged mixed relation. On divided powers the formulas are $E_{\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{-r(r-1)}K^rE_{\rm lib}^{(r)}$ and $F_{\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{r(r-1)}F_{\rm lib}^{(r)}K^{-r}$; the inverse formulas also have Laurent-monomial coefficients, so the integral lattice and toral generators are preserved.

The Lusztig specialization includes all divided powers $E^{(r)},F^{(r)}$ and the toral quantum binomials; this is the divided-power form, not the small quantum group. A finite-dimensional module is **type 1** when it carries its integral-weight grading $M=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}M_m$ with $K|_{M_m}=q^m$, the full toral character $T_{c,t}|_{M_m}=\begin{bmatrix}m+c\\t\end{bmatrix}_q I$ for every $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$, and $E^{(r)}M_m\subseteq M_{m+2r}$, $F^{(r)}M_m\subseteq M_{m-2r}$. The binomial is its Laurent-polynomial specialization, including negative upper indices. The grading is part of the data and is not collapsed when distinct weights have the same $K$ eigenvalue. Every module intertwiner preserves it: for $m<n$, $T_{-m,n-m}$ has eigenvalues $0$ and $1$ on weights $m$ and $n$.

For $a\ge0$, the Weyl module $\Delta(a)$ has basis $v_0,\ldots,v_a$ and actions

$$Kv_j=q^{a-2j}v_j,\qquad E^{(r)}v_j=\begin{bmatrix}a-j+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_qv_{j-r},\qquad F^{(r)}v_j=\begin{bmatrix}j+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_qv_{j+r},$$

where the Gaussian binomials are the Laurent-polynomial specializations of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], and $v_j=0$ outside $0\le j\le a$. 1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

to its bottom boundary points by the identity pairing in the blackboard
framing, with every band colored by $X$. Denote by
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ the value of the tangle evaluation functor
on a word in the elementary generators representing this closed diagram. Then

$$t_n(\beta)=F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

where $t_n$ is the ribbon trace of
[[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]] and $F_X$ is the tangle

[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]].

$\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}}$, and the blackboard-framed closure of the positive
stabilization $\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n$ is the framed closure of $\beta$ with
one positive curl added on a band, while the closure of the negative
stabilization adds one negative curl; with Turaev's convention the positive
curl is the generator $\varphi_X$ with $F_X(\varphi_X)=\theta_X$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals, twist $\theta$
([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) and Drinfeld morphism
$u_X\colon X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ of
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Put

$$j_X:=u_X\,\theta_X\ \colon\ X\longrightarrow X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Then $j$ is a natural isomorphism: it is the composite of the natural

X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\to(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$ of the double-dual

$$j_{X\otimes Y}=d_{X,Y}\circ(j_X\otimes j_Y),$$

which is precisely the statement that $u\theta$ is the pivotal comparison
induced by the ribbon structure; the identity follows from the tensor relation

the Drinfeld morphism together with the twist axiom
$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and

$$t_n(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_L\!\left(j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)\right)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

[[def-the-categorical-trace-of-a-morphism-into-the-double-dual]]: the composite

$X^{\otimes n}\to(X^{\otimes n})^{\vee\vee}$, which is exactly the input type of

[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]] is

trace, carries the choice cost.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) with
chosen left duals ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]), braiding $c$
([[def-braiding]]) and twist $\theta$, and let $X\in\mathcal C$. Write
$X_{+1}:=X$ and $X_{-1}:=X^{\vee}$. In a strict model of $\mathcal C$
([[thm-every-braided-monoidal-category-is-monoidally-equivalent-to-a-strict-braided-one]])
there is a unique strict monoidal functor

$$F_X\colon\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal C$$

from the framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ with

$$F_X(+)=X,\qquad F_X(-)=X^{\vee},$$

$$F_X\bigl(X^{+}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=c_{X_\varepsilon,X_{\varepsilon'}},\qquad F_X\bigl(X^{-}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=(c_{X_{\varepsilon'},X_\varepsilon})^{-1},\qquad F_X(\cup_{+1})=\operatorname{coev}_X,\qquad F_X(\cap_{+1})=\operatorname{ev}_X,\qquad F_X(\varphi^{\pm1}_{+1})=\theta_X^{\pm1},$$

where the cup and cap are the coevaluation and evaluation maps attached to the
chosen left duals and the signs are the blackboard conventions of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]]. The remaining elementary tangles
of $\mathcal T$, those carrying a negative sign at a cup, cap or twist, receive
the values forced by these data through the relations. Explicitly put
$j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, with $u$ as in
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Then

$$F_X(\cup_-)=(1_{X^\vee}\otimes j_X^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee},\qquad F_X(\cap_-)=\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}(j_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}),\qquad F_X(\varphi_-^{\pm1})=\theta_{X^\vee}^{\pm1}.$$

structure; they need no identification $X^{\vee\vee}=X$ on objects. For a general ribbon
category the same assignment determines a strong monoidal functor, unique up to
the canonical coherence isomorphisms of the strictification. Isotopic framed
tangles are equal morphisms of $\mathcal T$, so $F_X$ is an invariant of framed
tangles. Uniqueness needs no choice.

Thus the self-duality sign is $-1$, independently of rescaling. Put $e=wb$ and $U=-e=\delta P_0$. The snakes give $U_i^2=\delta U_i$, $U_iU_{i+1}U_i=U_i$ and distant commutation, so they give every $\rho_n$. The two channels and their twists/crossings are exactly [F1]. In particular $T=qU-1=-s c^{-1}$, so $q^2$ belongs to the trivial channel, not to the highest-weight-$2$ channel.

The rigid tensor functor from $\mathrm{TL}(-\delta)$ sends cup to $w$, cap to $b$, and $e_i$ to $w_ib_i$. The two snakes and negative loop verify its defining matching relations. The algebra identification $U_i\mapsto-e_i$ preserves the JW projectors: the recursion quantum integers for loop $-\delta$ are $(-1)^{j-1}[j]$, and these signs cancel against the generator sign in each recursive correction. Thus the evaluated projector $p_a$ is annihilated by the matrices $U_i$. For $a\le\ell-1$, their common kernel in each weight space is one-dimensional: $U_i$ imposes that the coefficient of $-+$ is $q$ times that of $+-$, so adjacent swaps determine every coefficient from one word. The vectors $F^{(j)}v_+^{\otimes a}$, $0\le j\le a$, belong to this kernel and are nonzero: the divided coproduct has one Laurent-monomial coefficient for every specified subset of $j$ changed positions. The projector acts as identity on its common kernel, since its nonidentity generator words kill that kernel. Its image is therefore precisely this $(a+1)$-dimensional highest-weight string, equal to $\Delta(a)$ by [F4]. In particular $p_{\ell-1}$ has a nonzero image of zero pivotal dimension, and cannot lie in the kernel of the unreduced map.

In the quantum negligible quotient the boundary image is zero by [F4]. Transport [F2]'s path splits to the negative-loop category. Its down normalization is $-\lambda_a$ rather than $\lambda_a=[a+1]/[a]$; replacing its down cap map by its negative yields exactly the positive-algebra normalization for $U=-e$. The transported path units therefore have the same multiplication and positive-$K$ trace weights $[a+1]$. They decompose $V^{\otimes n}$ into all retained $\Delta(a)$ copies. Hom orthogonality in [F4] shows their rectangular blocks are the **entire** quantum quotient Hom spaces, not a proper subalgebra. Their positive trace weights show independence, while [F2] identifies the diagram kernel as exactly $I_n$. This proves the displayed centralizer isomorphism. On a chosen retained sum $R_n$, composites through discarded negligible summands are zero because its weighted matrix-trace pairing is nondegenerate. Thus projecting to $R_n$ realizes the same algebra as $\operatorname{End}_U(R_n)$; the quotient formulation is independent of that choice.

The same path decomposition on both ends gives fullness and faithfulness for Hom spaces between unequal tensor degrees as well. Every tilting is a sum of summands of powers of $V$ by [F4]. The parity map $\epsilon_n=(-1)^n1_n$ is a monoidal natural automorphism: Hom spaces between different parities are zero. It descends to summands with $\epsilon_{p_a}=(-1)^a$ and commutes with duality. Thus $j=\epsilon j_0$ has the positive dimensions $[a+1]$. More precisely, the equality $KB^t=-B$ in step 1.1 says the functor's transported planar pivotal map on $V$ is $-K$; multiplying it by $\epsilon_V=-1$ gives exactly $K$. Monoidality, direct sums and summands prove equality of pivotal structures on every object, not merely equality of dimensions.
